data.why: The repo's own Data_Analysis/inhibitors.csv is 3.1MB (single long line, far over the 200KB budget), so a small synthetic table with the same single-cell FLIM feature schema (NADH/FAD Lifetime fit, Lifetime fit free-style bookkeeping, Intensity morphology/texture, a redox-ratio derived feature, cell_line/treatment/dish categoricals) was written instead, including a missing value, an outlier (t1=4.8 ns and t1=0.015 ns), to exercise the app's review/validation path.

goals: Upload a single-cell feature table and confirm the app correctly infers row ID, categorical, and numerical column roles
Review and correct any misdetected column roles or feature groups using the column editor
Compare NADH and FAD lifetime features (t1, t2, a1, tm) and redox ratio across cell lines and treatments using feature histograms and feature comparison plots
Build a phasor plot from the lifetime components to separate free vs. bound NADH populations
Reduce dimensionality (e.g. UMAP) across the feature set to see whether treatment groups separate
Export a standalone Python script that reproduces the analysis for later reuse

review.summary: The tree describes the parts of FLIM Playground's Data Analysis it reached accurately and at a sensible depth, and the screens I opened back nearly every node. But it wrongly says there is no phasor module: the module is hidden because the synthetic table left out the G/S columns the repo's own example has. It also misses filtering and figure export and folds two features into one, so it needs those fixes before it is filed.
